newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish paint maker seeks Q4 bourse entry.
newsitem.headline: Polish paint maker seeks Q4 bourse entry.

text.p: Polish paint maker Polifarb Debica SA plans a public offering of 500,000 to 700,000 shares and hopes to enter the Warsaw bourse before year-end, the company's legal head said.
"We plan to issue 500,000 to 700,000 shares -- our intention is to join the firms already listed on the bourse...before the end of the year," Aleksander Panek told Reuters.
The company has said it seeks a main-market listing.
Polifarb Debica shareholders must first approve the issue and the Polish Securities Commission (KPW) must approve the shares for public trade.
National Investment Fund (NFI) No. 11 in Poland's mass privatisation programme currently holds a 33-percent stake in Polifarb Debica.
Under the programme shares in some 500 companies are allocated to 15 NFIs run by domestic and international management firms.
Poland's 28.5 million adults are entitled to buy NFI units units which will be later exchanged for the shares in the individual funds.
